liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Mighty Quinn (Quinn The Eskimo)** (2 reviews): Opening with this track is considered a rare treasure; Starting the show with this track is praised as a nice treat [18][20]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Bobby's vocal performance is described as sounding like a squealed chicken [21]
- **Loser** (1 review): Billy and Mickey are too active, reducing the song's impact [21]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): The performance of this song is described as ripping [17]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): The energetic performance of this song is highlighted as a gem [18]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 review): Jerry forgot the ending chorus, repeating a line instead of the final phrase [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mardis Gras Parade**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-03-03.150141.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1987-03-03.166931.OaklandCA.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1648**: soundboard; 19 songs; 141 min [2]
- **gd1987-03-03.sbd-mtx.walker-scotton.miller.82725.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 136 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [5]
- **gd1987-03-03.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.82726.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 136 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [6]. Said about its sound: The reviewer claims Jerry sounds terrible and the performance is awful; The transfer is praised for great sound and few mistakes [25][26]
- **gd87-03-03.sbd.ladner.9175.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 130 min; rated 3.64/5 by 10 [14]. Said about its sound: The recording is noted for having nice sound quality [20]

## Around the show

- Bob Dylan attended to pose for Herb Greene before watching the first songs [16]
- Dylan left early to catch a plane back to Los Angeles [16]
- The listener drove alone from Los Angeles and gave away spare tickets [24]
- The basement bar at the Kaiser venue was described as cool [24]
- The Neville Brothers joined the band during the Iko Iko section [1]
- The Neville Brothers participated in the Mardi Gras Parade during Iko Iko [2]
- The Neville Brothers joined the band during the Iko Iko performance [5]
- The Neville Brothers joined the band during the Iko Iko performance [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-03-03.150141.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 22, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [1]
- **gd1987-03-03.166931.OaklandCA.sbd.cm.miller.t-flac1648**: taped by Ramrod Shurtliff's masters; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 2, 2024; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D56TDK SA-X) [2]. Also: These are Ramrod Shurtliff's masters, using multiple soundboard sources [2]
- **gd1987-03-03.sbd-mtx.walker-scotton.miller.82725.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) [5]. Also: This is a Matrix SBD, with thanks to Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [5]
- **gd1987-03-03.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.82726.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) [6]. Also: Thanks to Paul Scotton and Joani Walker for providing the tapes [6]
- **gd87-03-03.sbd.ladner.9175.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > DAT > CDR [14]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center - March 3, 1987](https://www.dead.net/show/march-3-1987) [28]
